experiments.description: Noisy scalar recurrent convergence across mixed contraction difficulty; compare fixed depth with local adaptive halt (2 consecutive |delta|<0.018 after step 3, max 32).
experiments.interpretation: Adaptive stopping occupied a different accuracy/compute point: lower MSE than fixed 16 while using about 9.15 mean steps, but fixed 24/32 achieved lower MSE at higher compute. This validates measuring a frontier, not declaring adaptive halting universally superior.

experiments.description: Forecast a latent process with slow AR(0.995) + fast AR(0.35) components. Compare best single EMA state against a two-timescale state with linear readout.
experiments.interpretation: On this deliberately heterogeneous process, two-timescale state improved test MSE by about 6.62%. This is a positive-control for the measurement idea, not evidence that FRANK gains 6.62%.

experiments.description: Sparse 10,000-node DAG; sample 1,000 changed source nodes and count descendants requiring recomputation.
experiments.interpretation: Sparse dependency structure can make incremental recomputation dramatically cheaper in operation count. Real FRANK affected-set density and maintenance overhead must be measured before claiming speedup.

experiments.description: 100,000 random child effect requests against explicit parent grants; compare ambient requested effects with a broker that intersects child effects with parent grant.
experiments.interpretation: The set-inclusion invariant is internally testable and the toy broker enforces it by construction. This is a contract sanity test only; it does not establish FFI/OS mediation completeness.
